headline: A strong storm brings rain and northeast gusts up to about 40–45 mph to Charlotte and the region tonight into Thanksgiving morning under a Wind Advisory until 10 AM Thursday, though rain totals and the flood risk keep trending down.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Rain has stayed very light so far Wednesday evening around Charlotte, but it will spread across the whole region and become nearly certain everywhere by midnight, staying warm enough for all rain. Northeast winds are already gusting up to 40 mph, and the Wind Advisory continues until 10 AM Thursday, with gusts probably no stronger than 45 mph away from the highest mountain peaks (mountain valleys in the Tennessee-border counties and Buncombe County are left out because the strongest gusts there stay above 3,500 feet). Gusts can blow over holiday decorations, tents, canopies and outdoor cookers (keep a fire extinguisher handy) and cause a few power outages. Expected rain amounts have dropped because the storm's center should track farther east; locally heavy rain is still possible mainly along and east of I-77, but the flood risk is low (a Marginal, level 1 of 4, risk), aside from some poor-drainage flooding where leaves clog storm drains.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: On Thanksgiving morning the storm passes nearby to the east, winds drop off noticeably for a while, and rain tapers off from south to north late morning into early afternoon, with winds turning west-southwest around noon to 3 PM. Low clouds hang on Thursday, possibly dropping very low over the Piedmont in the afternoon and evening, before improving late in the day, though a gray low-cloud deck may linger Thursday night into Friday. Gusts return by early evening Thursday around Charlotte and the Upstate and stay frequent through Friday until around sunset, but only at 25 to 35 mph, below advisory level, with no new advisory planned. Thursday evening, rain wrapping around the storm turns to snow showers along the Tennessee border, with an inch or less of snow there while areas east of the mountain crest likely stay dry; Friday is cold, about 10 degrees below normal, feeling like a typical winter day.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: High pressure brings a quieter, clearer Saturday with temperatures warming back to normal. A strong storm passes well to the northwest across the Midwest and Great Lakes Sunday into Monday morning, sending a weakening cold front through Sunday night or early Monday with a brief shot of rain; chances may be somewhat higher than some guidance shows, but amounts should stay under a quarter inch everywhere except southwest North Carolina. Temperatures stay near normal from Monday on.

watch_for: Wind gusts up to 40–45 mph until 10 AM Thursday — secure decorations, tents and outdoor cookers.
Any westward shift in the storm's track, which could bring heavier rain back into play east of I-77.
Snow showers near the Tennessee border Thursday evening, with up to an inch possible.
confidence: Forecasters say the overall storm scenario is on track and the winds through Thursday morning are behaving as expected, while rain amounts depend on the storm's exact track and confidence is low on how low the clouds get Thursday; the rest of the period looks relatively benign.
